goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Compare active-inference, model-free RL and model-based RL explanations of the original choices. Sensor/source EEG associations remain supporting descriptive outcomes; stronger significance cannot count as improved behavioral modeling.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Compare active-inference, model-free RL and model-based RL explanations of the original choices. Sensor/source EEG associations remain supporting descriptive outcomes; stronger significance cannot count as improved behavioral modeling.

Source-paper comparison for Original Figure 4c behavioral Bayesian information criterion (BIC), with original cohort and likelihood convention: BIC is the published ordered metric. Freeze its exact likelihood, sample-size convention and effective parameter count before scoring; fitting-notebook output and supplied-fit forward error are not automatically Figure 4c BIC.
success_criteria: Recover original Figure 4c BIC values and the publication-compatible active-inference/RL likelihood, parameter-count and aggregation conventions.
Compare the complete original behavioral cohort on the same choice-estimation task, with all method-selection and public-exposure limits declared.
Keep the canonical EEG outputs as descriptive/calibration evidence; do not claim their larger correlations or smaller p-values are a paper win.
A new held-out predictive split or a 23-person behavioral subset is an extension, not a source-paper victory.
Predeclare candidate freeze, meaningful effect, uncertainty and fixed budgets; forward-conformance success alone is never scientific success.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
